Answer the following multiple choice question. The last line of your response should be in the following format: 'Answer: A/B/C/D/E/F/G/H/I/J' (e.g. 'Answer: G').

A man dies without a will in a jurisdiction that recognizes no statutory framework for body disposition. His brother and sister, both equally related and surviving, disagree on whether to bury or cremate the body. The sister, who had cared for him during his final illness, takes possession of the body and proceeds with cremation. The brother sues, seeking an injunction to halt the cremation and a declaration that he shares equal rights. What is the likely outcome?

A) The brother prevails, because rights to the body are joint among all next of kin.  
B) The sister prevails, because she had physical possession and acted in good faith.  
C) The brother prevails, because cremation requires unanimous consent.  
D) The sister prevails, because the right to possession is exclusive and belongs to the closest next of kin, but kinship is equal here.  
E) The court will appoint an administrator to decide, because no clear legal rule applies.  
F) The brother prevails, because burial is the default unless otherwise indicated.  
G) The sister prevails, because emotional attachment grants superior legal rights.  
H) The brother prevails, because he filed the lawsuit first.  
I) The sister prevails, because she incurred the burial expenses.  
J) The court will split the remains, as a matter of equitable division.
